entries.topic: Native phased inputs, marker support and map
entries.paper_statement: Official FLARE documentation requires phased, nonmissing genotypes, a reference panel and a PLINK genetic map in cM. Multiple ALT alleles are supported.
entries.release_or_adapter_finding: AdmixReader joins exact CHROM, POS, REF and ALT, filters reference panel membership, rejects overlap between reference and study IDs, and applies a minimum to the second-largest reference allele count. Our converter keeps all sites and original phased pairing. Its uniform map spans 30 cM over 30 Mb. An unused BitArray overload writes the first allele twice; the native reference-record route uses phasedAlleles and nonMajAlleleIndices instead.
entries.execution_route: Official native Java ancestry route, with optional panel-probability workflow separated.
entries.resolution: Supported native inputs are resolved. There is no demonstrated active converter or native parser defect. Do not invent a biallelic-only restriction or lower the native MAC threshold.

entries.paper_statement: Official gen=10 is an initial value when em=true. The default is update-p=false.

entries.paper_statement: Native AN1 and AN2 report the most probable ancestry. Optional ANP1 and ANP2 contain rounded posterior vectors. The ARGformer paper does not give a marker-to-focal projection rule.
entries.release_or_adapter_finding: Native hard calls use unrounded probabilities, with the first ancestry index winning exact ties. Our adapter preserves AN1 and AN2 and remaps the ancestry header to the frozen class order. It projects to nearest marker midpoints, assigns midpoint ties to the right and carries endpoint calls to the domain edges. Raw rounded ANP vectors and strings remain unchanged.
entries.execution_route: Official native Java ancestry route, with optional panel-probability workflow separated.
entries.resolution: Native call semantics are resolved. Projection is an explicit study choice. Do not replace native calls with argmax of rounded ANP or describe one-hot transport as posterior probabilities.
